item.text: The repository is intentionally bare: there’s no database or user model to integrate with. I’m treating the preference as per-user browser state via a server-written cookie, which gives the demo real persistence across requests while keeping all reads and writes server-side; the action will then call `refresh()` from `next/cache`, with no redirect.

item.text:
Implemented the notification toggle without redirects.

- [app/actions.ts](/workspace/app/actions.ts:10) defines the Server Action, persists the inverse preference, then calls `refresh()` from `next/cache`—the [recommended Next.js API](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/refresh) for refreshing the current page.
- [app/notification-preference.ts](/workspace/app/notification-preference.ts:5) stores the per-user preference in a secure, HTTP-only cookie because this repository has no database or authentication layer.
- [app/page.tsx](/workspace/app/page.tsx:4) reads the current preference server-side and submits the toggle through a form action.

Verification passed:

- Production build
- TypeScript check
- Runtime toggle `off → on → off`
- Each submission returned HTTP 200 on `/`, with no redirect.
